subject: Procurement sequencing and MAP: proposed three-lane close cadence
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixcare.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@helixcare.com
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement sequencing and MAP for HelixCare pilot

Hi Mina / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at HelixCare has asked us to put together a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out sequencing for the pilot signature path — specifically they want clarity on whether the Order Form, MSA and DPA will be signed together or in phases.

High level from HelixCare: they prefer to get the PO / Order Form in place quickly so engineering can start the provisioning work, but legal has flagged the DPA as a gating item for any data flows beyond anonymized telemetry.

I attached a first-pass MAP (HelixCare_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a draft Order Form. Proposed, high-level options:
- Option A: Sign Order Form (and PO) first; onboarding work starts; MSA & DPA follow (staggered).
- Option B: Parallel signature — Order Form + MSA together; DPA as an attachable schedule to MSA but executed within 10 business days.
- Option C: Management lane — temporary data flow restrictions until DPA signed (slower).

Can you outline Redwood’s recommended sequencing and call out the minimum legal evidence you need from us to unblock the DPA review? Procurement would like a short MAP with dates so they can internal-approve a 3-week pilot start window.

Attachments: HelixCare_MAP_v1.xlsx; OrderForm_Draft.pdf

Appreciate a quick turnaround — Samantha
Samantha Lee
Senior Procurement Manager, HelixCare
S: +1 415-555-0192

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixcare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement sequencing and MAP for HelixCare pilot

Thanks Samantha — good, pragmatic framing. Looping Laura from Legal so we can be explicit about the DPA gating items.

Short answer: Redwood is flexible across two safe patterns but we need to call out tradeoffs. Suggested recommendation for your MAP: a three-lane cadence (we'll call it "order-first with DPA lane"), which gives procurement the ability to approve an order and start technical onboarding while preserving a hard stop for any data-in-transit that needs contractual protections.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) Day 0: Order Form & PO approved and countersigned (HelixCare procurement sign-off).
2) Day 3–7: Provisioning & technical onramp begin (restricted to non-PI telemetry).
3) Day 7–14: DPA redline exchange; HelixCare legal provides third-party vendor review window if needed.
4) Day 14–21: DPA execution and full data flows enabled; MSA signature can be parallel or immediately after DPA execution depending on terms.

Key asks from HelixCare to make this safe for both sides:
- A list of categories of data types you anticipate (PI, pseudonymous telemetry, logs).
- Any internal regulatory review timeline (e.g., third-party privacy office review).
- Confirmation whether a provisional DPA (placeholder language) would be accepted to unblock engineering.

I'll attach a short note with redline pointers and an internal risk callout (redline-pointers.txt). Laura — can you flag anything else we should require as evidence before we allow non-anonymized data flows?

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: sequencing risk matrix + recommended gating steps (HelixCare)

Mina / Laura — quick internal note before I respond to Samantha with a clean MAP document. I sketched a minimal risk matrix and sequencing recommendations:

Risk scenarios and recommended gating:
- Risk: Order Form signed, provisioning starts, DPA delayed > 3 weeks -> Exposure if non-anonymized data flows begin.
  Mitigation: Technical isolation and access controls; explicit checklist for what provisioning can and cannot do before DPA (we should require a written confirmation from HelixCare that initial provisioning will not include PHI/PI).

- Risk: DPA signed but MSA contains open indemnity/limitation terms -> Business disagreement later.
  Mitigation: Allow MSA signature with a narrow clause tying unresolved commercial terms to an escrow or holdback (legal-opt).

Recommended MAP gating steps to include in the document we send back to HelixCare:
1) Procurement lane: Order Form (sign) -> Procurement confirms PO and billing contact.
2) Compliance lane: HelixCare provides data categories + expected data recipients -> Redwood provides required evidence list (SOC2 report, subprocessor list, data retention policy).
3) Legal lane: DPA redline exchange with 10 business day review; if external vendor review needed, slot an additional 5-day buffer.

I will draft a single-page MAP that maps these three lanes to dates (0/3/7/14/21) and call out fallback where we only allow anonymized telemetry until DPA executes. Once Laura confirms the evidence list, I'll send to Samantha with the draft Order Form attached.

-Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixcare.com>

Thanks — that approach sounds workable. Procurement can prioritize the Order Form sign and provide a PO within 5 business days if Redwood confirms the provisioning scope won't include PHI/PI until DPA execution.

Action items from HelixCare side:
- We will deliver the Procurement Questionnaire (attached) and a short data type inventory by EOD Thursday.
- Our legal team will do an initial DPA review — they have indicated they may need a week plus any vendor privacy office slot. We appreciate Redwood providing a concise evidence list (SOC 2 latest, subprocessor list, retention policy) and a sample minimal DPA with standard vendor-friendly language.

We are comfortable with the three-lane MAP you described. Please send the one-page MAP with dates and the redline pointers so procurement can calendar-approve.

Attachments: HelixCare_Procurement_Questionnaire.docx

Thanks,
Samantha
